subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Read a model email and find how it covers all four points.
Give advice and suggestions with different phrases.
Plan, write and check an informal email of about 100 words.

tf.s: Jood's email is informal: it starts with Hi and uses contractions.
tf.why: These features show an informal style.

tf.s: Jood's reply covers all four points from her notes.
tf.why: A good reply includes every note.

tf.s: A good reply only repeats the notes word for word.
tf.why: Jood adds a little extra information to each note.

tf.s: 'I think you ought to help a local business go digital' gives advice.
'I hope you're feeling better now' gives advice.
We say 'You ought help with a recycling project.'
tf.why: We need 'to': You ought to help.

tf.s: Razan wrote a letter, not an email.
Using different advice phrases makes your email more interesting.
tf.why: A range of language shows your skills.

tf.s: Your reply to Khalid should be about 100 words.
tf.why: The task asks for about 100 words.

tf.s: Checking spelling and punctuation is part of improving your email.

boxes.q: Complete: ___ don't you offer to help people with their devices?
boxes.why: Why don't you ...? makes a suggestion.

boxes.q: Complete: How about ___ people set up websites?
Complete: ___ I send you some information about the hospital?
boxes.why: Shall I ...? offers to do something.

boxes.q: Complete: I think you ___ phone them.
How many points from the notes must your email include?
boxes.why: There are four notes to cover.

boxes.q: Why is Arwa writing to Jood?
o: to ask about Teen Tech Help Month
to invite her to a party
boxes.why: She asks which project is better and how she can help.

boxes.q: Which greeting shows an informal email?

o: start using technology and the internet
boxes.why: A business goes digital when it uses technology.

o: an organisation that helps people in need
a type of shop that sells phones
boxes.why: Charities help people, animals or the environment.

mcq.q: Which features make Jood's email informal?
o: Hi, contractions and an exclamation mark

mcq.q: Which phrase in Jood's email gives advice?
o: I think you ought to help a local business go digital.
I hope you're feeling better now.
Something like a local café or bakery.

mcq.q: How many paragraphs does Jood's email have?
mcq.why: Each of the three paragraphs has a clear purpose.

mcq.q: What is the purpose of 'I hope you're feeling better now'?
mcq.why: It shows care for the reader.

mcq.q: Correct the mistake: 'You ought help with a recycling project.'
o: You ought to help with a recycling project.
You ought helping with a recycling project.
You ought to helping with a recycling project.
You ought helped with a recycling project.

mcq.q: Which is a good suggestion for Teen Tech Help Month?
o: You could teach older people to use their phones.
You could to teach older people.
Why you don't teach older people?

mcq.q: Which sentence gives advice to Razan about helping children?
o: You could read stories to children in the hospital.
You could reading stories to children.
mcq.why: You could + base verb gives a suggestion.

mcq.q: Why should you avoid repeating the same advice phrase?
o: To show a range of language and make the email interesting
Because the same phrase is wrong grammar

mcq.q: Jood writes 'Something like a local café or bakery.' What does this show?
o: She adds extra information, not just the notes
mcq.why: Adding details makes the reply richer.

mcq.q: What is the best order for writing your email?
o: Plan the four points, write about 100 words, then check it
mcq.why: Planning and checking make a strong email.
